overview: RELX is a London-headquartered (also listed Amsterdam and New York via ADR) global provider of information-based analytics and decision tools, operating through four segments: Risk (fraud/identity, insurance, business services), Scientific, Technical & Medical/STM (Elsevier journals, databases, AI research tools), Legal (LexisNexis legal research and analytics), and Exhibitions (Reed Exhibitions trade shows). The business model combines proprietary data sets, deep customer workflow integration, and increasingly AI-enabled analytics software layered over trusted content, sold mostly on subscription/transactional bases to professional, academic, corporate and government customers worldwide, with the US as its largest market.

business_model.summary: RELX monetizes large proprietary and contributory datasets and trusted content by embedding AI-enabled analytics and decision tools into customer workflows, generating high-margin, largely recurring subscription and transactional revenue; Exhibitions is a cyclical, event-driven complement. Group adjusted operating margin was 35.5% in H1 2026, up from 34.8% in H1 2025, with underlying revenue growth of +7% and underlying adjusted operating profit growth of +9%.
business_model.customer_type: B2B and B2G: financial institutions, insurers, corporates, law firms, researchers/academic institutions, government agencies, and trade-show exhibitors/visitors
business_model.geographic_mix: US is the largest single market; significant presence across UK/Europe, and growing exposure in Asia-Pacific (notably China exhibitions) and emerging markets; reports in GBP with material USD and EUR revenue/cost exposure

competitive_position.market_position: Global leader or co-leader in each of its four segments: top-tier legal research/analytics platform (LexisNexis, duopoly with Thomson Reuters' Westlaw), largest academic STM publisher (Elsevier, ~2,900 journals), a leading risk-analytics/fraud-and-identity provider (LexisNexis Risk Solutions), and one of the largest global B2B exhibition organizers (Reed Exhibitions)

moat_factors.description: Decades-accumulated contributory databases (e.g., insurance claims, fraud signals) and the Elsevier corpus of scientific literature and citation data (Scopus) are difficult for new entrants to replicate
Legal research (Lexis+ AI with Protégé agentic assistant), risk decisioning, and researcher tools are deeply embedded in daily customer workflows, creating high switching costs
Contributory data models in Risk (insurance, fraud) and citation/usage networks in STM improve with scale and more contributors
LexisNexis, Elsevier and Reed Exhibitions are long-established, trusted brands in their respective professional markets

Management cites AI (e.g., Scopus AI, Sherpath AI, LeapSpace, Lexis+ AI/Protégé) as both a growth driver and a way to keep cost growth below revenue growth, though AI also lowers barriers for new entrants

weaknesses: STM segment exposed to a structural shift from subscription ('pay-to-read') to open-access ('pay-to-publish') models and to research funding cycles
Exhibitions is inherently cyclical and exposed to travel disruption, geopolitics (e.g., Middle East events) and pandemics
Generative AI and large language models could, over time, erode the value of some proprietary content/IP if not continually defended and enhanced
High financial leverage used to fund buybacks and bolt-on M&A

growth_drivers: Continued shift in business mix toward higher-growth, higher-value AI-enabled analytics and decision tools across all four segments
Legal: adoption of Lexis+ AI with the agentic Protégé assistant driving double-digit underlying growth
STM: AI tools (Scopus AI, Sherpath AI, LeapSpace) and strong article-submission volume growth
Risk: expansion of Financial Crime Compliance, digital Fraud & Identity, and contributory insurance databases
Bolt-on M&A in AI/legaltech and identity verification (e.g., IDVerse acquisition completed; Doctrine acquisition announced/pending) supplementing organic growth
Exhibitions: digital tools for exhibitors/attendees and recovery/growth of face-to-face event portfolio
Ongoing share buybacks (£2,250m program for 2026, ~£1,750m completed in H1) supporting EPS growth
Progressive dividend policy (~50% payout of adjusted EPS) with 7% H1 2026 dividend growth

business.description: Shift from pay-to-read to pay-to-publish (open access) and research integrity/fraudulent paper detection risk could affect STM revenue mix and growth
Rapid AI and workflow-tool innovation could change customer demand patterns; failure to adapt products/pricing could hurt revenue
AI and technology tools used by competitors could infringe or circumvent IP protections, pressuring product demand/pricing
Economic cycles, travel disruption (e.g., ongoing Middle East uncertainty), pandemics, and natural disasters can reduce Exhibitions revenue and increase costs
Bolt-on M&A (IDVerse, pending Doctrine deal) may not deliver anticipated revenue growth, cost synergies, or could trigger goodwill/intangible impairment
Competing globally for scarce AI, data analytics and technology talent

financial.description: Net debt grew to £8,733m at H1 2026 (net debt/EBITDA 2.3x) from £7,443m a year earlier, driven by buybacks and acquisitions, partly offset by strong cash conversion (98%)
Reports in GBP but earns/costs substantially in USD, EUR and JPY; FX reduced H1 2026 reported revenue growth by ~2 points
Average interest rate on gross debt was 3.6% in H1 2026; a ratings downgrade could raise borrowing costs
Legacy UK and US DB pension schemes (UK closing to accruals in 2027) remain sensitive to discount rates, inflation and longevity assumptions

regulatory.description: Risk and other segments rely extensively on personal data from public records and other sources; tightening privacy law/enforcement globally could restrict data collection/use and product availability

regulatory.risk: Cross-border and antitrust scrutiny of IP/tech
regulatory.description: EU and other jurisdictions' legislative/judicial initiatives could weaken IP protections relevant to content and AI-trained products

regulatory.risk: Tax law changes / cross-border tax disputes
regulatory.description: Operates across many tax jurisdictions; ongoing discussions with tax authorities on cross-border transactions

macro.description: War, sanctions, political tensions, and US-Europe-China trade relations could affect demand and ability to operate internationally

macro.risk: Government and private research funding levels
macro.description: Potential cuts in government/funder support for scientific research (e.g., funder pullback from open-access publishing fees, universities declining Elsevier renewal terms) could pressure STM revenue
Risk, Legal and STM are largely non-discretionary/subscription-based and defensive, but Exhibitions and parts of Risk's business-services demand are more cyclical

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Information-based analytics/decision-tools markets (risk analytics, legal tech, scholarly publishing, B2B exhibitions) are seeing structural growth from the shift to higher-value analytics software and AI-enabled tools layered over proprietary data, a trend RELX management describes as having driven the business for over a decade and expected to continue
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low-to-moderate overall given subscription-heavy mix in Risk/STM/Legal (~88% of revenue), but Exhibitions (~12%) is cyclical and travel/geopolitics-sensitive
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — net debt/EBITDA of 2.3x and ongoing refinancing (e.g., €1.5bn of EUR term debt issued June 2026) make borrowing costs and credit rating relevant to EPS growth
key_input_costs: Content/data acquisition and contributory data costs

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 results: revenue £4,871m (+7% underlying), adjusted operating profit £1,727m (+9% underlying), adjusted EPS 68.6p (+11% constant currency); full-year outlook reaffirmed for strong underlying growth
Issued €1.5bn of EUR-denominated term debt (3-year at 3.25%, 8-year at 3.75%) to refinance/fund growth
Announced agreement to acquire Doctrine, a French legal-AI platform, to strengthen Legal segment AI capabilities (pending regulatory/consultation steps)
FY2025 full-year results reported; five small acquisitions totaling £270m completed in 2025, the most significant being IDVerse (document authentication/fraud detection, LexisNexis Risk)
Completed acquisition of IDVerse, adding to LexisNexis Risk Solutions' Business Services fraud and identity-verification capability

Continued rollout of AI products across segments: Lexis+ AI with agentic assistant Protégé (Legal, driving double-digit growth), Scopus AI, Sherpath AI and new research-grade AI workspace LeapSpace (STM)

Several UK universities (including Sheffield, Lancaster and Surrey) declined renewal of Elsevier's 2026 read-and-publish deal citing cost pressure, and some funders (e.g., Cancer Research UK) are cutting open-access publishing fee support — an emerging headwind for STM pricing/mix
Ongoing share buyback: £2,250m program for 2026 with £1,750m (69.2m shares at avg 2,529p) completed by end of H1, remaining ~£400-500m to be completed by year-end

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Erik Engstrom highlighted continued strong growth in Risk, a step-up in STM growth, a further step-up in Legal growth, and strong ongoing growth in Exhibitions. He emphasized that the shift in business mix toward higher-growth analytics and decision tools, combined with AI enabling faster product development and cost growth kept below revenue growth, is the key long-term driver of value and growth for the business.

bull_case: Diversified, largely subscription-based revenue (~88% ex-print/Exhibitions-cyclicality) across four structurally advantaged segments gives resilience plus multi-year double-digit growth pockets (Legal, Risk)

AI is a demonstrated net positive so far — embedding generative AI/agentic tools (Protégé, Scopus AI) into proprietary data has accelerated growth and margins rather than disrupting the moat, countering bear narratives about AI disintermediation
Consistent execution: underlying revenue growth accelerating across all four segments in H1 2026, margin expansion (35.5% vs 34.8%), strong cash conversion (98%) funding both buybacks and bolt-on M&A

Shareholder returns: ~£2.25bn 2026 buyback plus a progressive dividend (11th consecutive year of ~50% payout policy, AAA MSCI ESG rating for 11 years) supports total shareholder return even if multiple re-rating stalls
Strong analyst/consensus support (Strong Buy consensus, targets generally above current trading levels from BofA, Barclays, Goldman Sachs) reflecting confidence in the AI-enabled growth narrative
bear_case: STM faces a structural headwind as universities and funders (UK institutions, Cancer Research UK) push back on Elsevier pricing and open-access fee models, risking pressure on pay-to-publish economics and renewal terms
Rising net leverage (net debt/EBITDA up to 2.3x from 2.2x) driven by aggressive buybacks and M&A reduces financial flexibility if growth slows or rates stay elevated
Exhibitions remains exposed to geopolitical/travel disruption (management itself flagged Middle East event uncertainty) and is inherently more cyclical than the other three segments
Valuation already prices in a strong AI-driven growth story (premium multiples, Strong Buy consensus), leaving limited margin for execution missteps or a deceleration in Legal/Risk growth rates

Long-term risk that generative AI and large language models erode the pricing power of proprietary content/IP across legal and STM if competitors or open models narrow RELX's data/analytics advantage faster than it can innovate
